applied.name: tetrahydrofuran
applied.value: Another public table reports 7.6. Source-priority pass: neither NBS Circular 514 (all 636 transcribed organic rows checked) nor the 242-file local ThermoML corpus contains a tetrahydrofuran permittivity observation. A restricted SpringerMaterials record for THF agrees with this open value, but that source is non-redistributable and was used only as a cross-check. The open-access review-table provenance is therefore retained deliberately.
applied.rationale: Appendix I item G1-3 requires the THF source-priority decision to be documented instead of left as an unexplained downgrade.

applied.name: vinylene carbonate
applied.value: Conflict record: the stored 126 at 298 K comes from an open-access article text (10.1002/cssc.202402091) and is reproduced independently by the ECW-308 compilation (10.1002/adfm.202212342 Table S3, 126.00 at 25 C, citing Hall et al. and Flamme et al.). The row stays conflict_open because a Knovel Critical Tables-derived interval of 78-127 disagrees, and no primary measurement was found in NBS Circular 514, the 242-file local ThermoML corpus, PubChem, or NIST WebBook. Vinylene carbonate melts near 295 K, so the 298 K observation sits close to the melting point.
applied.rationale: The v0.3.2 hand-edit that restored this note stored it as unreadable replacement characters, and no readable version exists anywhere in git history. Replacing it with the evidence actually collected in the G1+ Tier 0-2 passes keeps the conflict auditable instead of preserving mojibake.
